$comment: QA-002 expected findings for the deliberately broken package corpus. Produced by tools/qa/skillpkg-corpus/generate.py, asserted by TestQA002BrokenPackageCorpus in apps/platform/internal/ingest. Every entry was reviewed against skillpkg.go, not recorded from a run: where the observed behaviour is weaker than the failure mode deserves, the entry says so in `gap` instead of being softened into a pass. The three `gap` entries v1 carried (zip-path-traversal, zip-absolute-path, zip-symlink-escape) were closed on 2026-08-18 by fixing the scanner, not by relaxing the expectation — those three now assert findings, and each entry's note keeps what the gap said.

asserted.archive_error: PackageFS is expected to refuse the archive (ErrBadArchive) before validation runs.
asserted.errors: exact set of distinct error codes
asserted.warnings: exact set of distinct warning codes
asserted.info_includes: subset — disclosure noise (external URLs, dependency lists) varies with each base package's content and is not what a blocking decision is made of

base-humanizer.breaks: nothing — legal sample, the not-falsely-blocked control
base-humanizer.note: Prompt-only writing skill that ships one validation script. A base that ever gains an error or warning code means either the base moved or the scanner did; both need a human, which is why this is an exact set and not a subset.

base-csv-to-json.breaks: nothing — legal sample, the not-falsely-blocked control
base-csv-to-json.note: Declares no license in frontmatter; the repacker carried the repo-level one in as LICENSE.repo (ADR-021 tier 3), so the license disclosure is expected rather than a defect.

base-excel-freeze.breaks: nothing — legal sample, the not-falsely-blocked control
base-excel-freeze.note: A legal package can carry a warning: this one's embedded Python imports openpyxl while the package ships no dependency manifest. Warning, not error — it does not block, and the corpus records that distinction rather than treating every finding as a rejection.

skill-md-missing.breaks: SKILL.md deleted from the package root
skill-md-missing.note: Validate returns immediately, so the tree is never walked and the package's script file is not disclosed. Correct: there is nothing to disclose it against.

frontmatter-missing.breaks: SKILL.md starts with prose, no `---` header
frontmatter-missing.note: Manifest stays nil, so the manifest, license, file-reference and embedded-code checks are all skipped while scanTree still runs. That is why no license-unknown warning appears here.

frontmatter-unterminated.note: The generator strips every bare `---` line from the body first. Without that, cutClosingDelimiter closes the header at the first horizontal rule and the variant reports frontmatter-invalid-yaml instead — a real behaviour, but not the one this entry is named after.

frontmatter-invalid-yaml.note: An unclosed flow sequence in the name field. Manifest stays nil for the same reason as frontmatter-missing.

name-missing.note: Name and description are checked independently, so a package missing only the name reports only that.

name-invalid.note: Uppercase, underscore and punctuation in one value. The rule is a single switch with the empty and over-long cases, so only one code can fire.

name-too-long.breaks: `name` is 65 runes, one over the cap
name-too-long.note: One over the boundary on purpose. The value is also rule-valid, so name-too-long has to win rather than name-invalid.

description-missing.note: License resolution still runs here — the manifest parsed, it is only a required field that is absent.

description-too-long.breaks: `description` is 1025 runes, one over the cap
description-too-long.note: Counted in runes, which is the fix import-report.md §6.1 bug 1 recorded; an ASCII value is therefore the weaker of the two tests and a zh-Hant one would be the stronger. This entry uses ASCII because the boundary itself is what is under test.

frontmatter-unknown-field.note: Deliberately not blocking: the Agent Skills spec evolves and an unknown key is a warning. The key chosen (`auto_run`) is the shape an author would use to try to claim a behaviour the platform does not honour.

file-ref-escapes.breaks: SKILL.md links to a path outside the package
file-ref-escapes.note: undeclared-dependency is inherited from the base, not caused by the mutation. Warning rather than error is the scanner's existing judgement: a document link cannot read anything by itself.

file-ref-missing.breaks: SKILL.md links to a file the package does not ship
file-ref-missing.note: The in-package counterpart of file-ref-escapes: same severity, different reason.

embedded-script.breaks: 60 lines of Python written into SKILL.md itself
embedded-script.note: The failure mode SKILL-003 exists for: the file list shows no such script, so an extension-only scan reports a package that contains none. 60 lines is over both thresholds (20 per block, 50 total).

binary-file.breaks: a compiled object nobody can review as text
binary-file.note: Warning, not error. package-dependencies drops out of the info set here relative to the base — the ELF header makes isBinary true for that file, which changes nothing about the dependency scan, but the base's own dependency evidence still stands. Asserted as a subset, so this entry does not pin it either way.

secret-in-script.breaks: an AWS access key id inside a shipped script
secret-in-script.note: Blocking, and the finding must never echo the matched value (NFR-002). The corpus value is assembled at runtime from parts so this repo's own pre-push credential grep cannot be tripped by the generator's source.

secret-in-skill-md.breaks: private key material pasted into SKILL.md
secret-in-skill-md.note: Same code from a different pattern and a different file — SKILL.md is scanned as part of the tree, not only parsed as a manifest.

zip-path-traversal.breaks: a zip entry whose name walks out of the package
zip-path-traversal.note: v1 recorded this as a gap: archive/zip's fs.FS rewrote `../../evil.sh` to `evil.sh` before anything in this codebase saw it, so the code set was byte-for-byte the clean base's. Closed 2026-08-18 (04 丙-15 D-1) — ingest.PackageFS now reads the raw zip.Reader entry names before fs.Sub and hands the findings to skillpkg. Still not a zip-slip (nothing extracts to disk); it blocks because an entry aimed outside the package is an attempt, and because the tree a reviewer approves has to be the tree the archive declares. The entry is also still visible as `evil.sh` in the tree, which is why script-file remains.

zip-absolute-path.breaks: a zip entry with an absolute path
zip-absolute-path.note: Same fix and the same code as zip-path-traversal (04 丙-15 D-2): one rule, one code, different message. v1's gap noted this one was quieter still — `/etc/cron.d/evil` becomes `etc/cron.d/evil`, which has no script extension, so not even an info-level disclosure appeared. info_includes stays empty on purpose.

zip-symlink-escape.breaks: a symlink entry pointing outside the package
zip-symlink-escape.note: v1 recorded a gap: the zip fs.FS presents the entry as an ordinary 11-byte file whose content is the target path, so the scan never said the package contained a link at all. Closed 2026-08-18 (04 丙-15 D-3) — the tree scan reads the entry's mode and discloses the link and its target. Warning and not error on purpose: packaging.travels() already refuses anything that is not a regular file, so a link never reaches a download (PACK-001's exclusion list is satisfied by exclusion), while blocking would reject import and every Run of a package carrying a benign link. What was missing was the disclosure, not a block.

zip-bomb.breaks: declared uncompressed size over the unpack cap
zip-bomb.note: 260 MiB of real zeros, not a doctored header: PackageFS reads the declared size out of the central directory, and a corpus that lied there would stop testing the cap the day that reader changes how it measures. Refused before Validate runs, so there is no report and no finding — the harness asserts ErrBadArchive instead.

oversize-file.breaks: a file above the content-scan size cap
oversize-file.note: Working as designed and worth pinning: a file over 1 MiB is disclosed as unscanned rather than silently skipped, which is what keeps 'no secret found' from meaning 'not looked at'.
